rationale: Microsoft Playwright is an S-tier browser automation framework and the core engine for a Veridian scraping pipeline. The repository contains 3,291 source files across 397 directories with a sophisticated client-server-dispatcher architecture connected by a formal RPC protocol (protocol.yml). It drives Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit via a unified API with auto-waiting, web-first assertions, resilient locators (role, text, testid, CSS, XPath), and built-in network interception (route, HAR, SOCKS proxy). It has a complete MCP tool layer with 34 backend tool files and 97 MCP test files, enabling AI-agent-driven browser automation (navigate, snapshot, click, fill, evaluate, extract). The proxy interception (socksInterceptor.ts, socksClientCertificatesInterceptor.ts) provides stealth capability. The selector generator (selectorGenerator.ts) supports role/text/testid locators approximating fuzzy matching for element resolution. Full ARIA snapshot extraction (ariaSnapshot.ts) is built into the injected package for structured page data. No JSON-LD extraction, queue/job scheduling, or fulltext search is present natively. Heritage is declared_prior per assignment — Playwright is a known foundational dependency for Veridian's browser automation layer. Tier S due to the codebase being the de-facto industry standard for cross-browser automation with comprehensive architecture docs, extensive tests (934 test files), robust MCP/AI integration, and direct relevance to every scraping pipeline step requiring browser interaction.
limitations: No JSON-LD / Schema.org extraction engine present. Playwright can navigate and extract page content but has no built-in JSON-LD parser.
No queue or job scheduling system — this is a browser automation library, not a job orchestrator.
No full-text search indexing capability — Playwright can read page text but does not index or search it.
No dedicated self-healing selector mechanism — locators auto-wait and retry (web-first assertions) but there is no historical selector fallback chain.
Stealth capabilities are limited to SOCKS proxy interception and certificate handling; no dedicated anti-bot fingerprint randomization beyond what browser context isolation provides.
Fuzzy matching is limited to attribute-based selectors (role, text, label) without Levenshtein or similarity-based element resolution.
